one: Build a language model from scratch: data cleaning, tokenizer, Transformer, training, scaling, evaluation, and deployment.
pos: CS 336 is one of the most hard-core LLM courses, taught by Percy Liang and Tatsunori Hashimoto. Inspired by 'build an OS from scratch', it walks through the full language-model lifecycle; the assignments need substantial GPU compute, and enrollment requires an application.
topics: **Model**: Transformer architecture, attention variants, positional encoding
**Training**: initialization, optimizers, learning rates, mixed precision, distributed training
**Safety and ethics**: data copyright, bias, misuse
prereq: Strong programming; deep learning background (CS 224N/CS 231N/CS 230 level); application required, GPU resources recommended.
assess: Typically about five programming assignments that build the LM step by step, plus a project; compute-heavy. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: People who want to understand the full LLM stack and later work on pre-training/inference/systems; founders building models.
tips: Take CS 224N or CS 231N first. Without GPUs you can run small models, but the assignment experience will be limited.
